no looking at the code at all
For security work I've found that having Claude review GPT's work, and vice-versa, really does work surprisingly well.

The problem is it really does work—I’ve started habitually having Anthropic’s best model review OpenAI’s work and vice versa, because I’ve had that turn up interesting results often enough to be valuable.

Sometimes this involves reviewing every line of code they have written, but there are other ways to achieve that goal. Eyeballing every line of code has never been the most effective way to validate a change to a piece of software.
Don't file pull requests with code you haven't reviewed yourself.
